name: Co-working spaces
shape_facts: Number of locations, total desks/offices, and meeting rooms
Membership mix: hot desks, dedicated desks, private offices, virtual office/business address, day passes
Typical members (freelancers, startups, SMEs, remote corporate teams)
Lease structure with the landlord and fit-out situation
Staff on site (community manager, front desk, cleaners, IT)
Systems used for bookings, billing and access (spreadsheets, booking software, door access system)
Extra services sold (printing, events, mail, licensing support in UAE)
scope_rule: pi notes the operator’s business and operational problems: occupancy and sales, enquiries and tours, bookings, billing and collections, member experience, facilities and maintenance, staff, access control and reporting. pi gives no real estate, lease, legal, tax or building-safety-engineering advice, and never takes members’ names, IDs, company details, access codes or Wi-Fi passwords. It records member types and counts only. Requests to issue fake tenancy contracts or addresses for visa purposes, monitor members covertly, or bypass building safety rules are declined; any fire, gas, electrical or medical emergency goes to emergency services.

vocabulary.Hot desk: any free desk, no fixed seat
vocabulary.Virtual office: business address and mail handling without a desk
vocabulary.Occupancy: share of desks or offices currently sold
vocabulary.Membership agreement: contract with a member, usually month-to-month or fixed term
vocabulary.Community manager: staff who runs member relations and events
vocabulary.Credits: included meeting-room hours or printing allowance
vocabulary.Tour: showing a prospect around the space
vocabulary.Flexi desk: UAE desk package often used to meet licence office requirements

problems.phrase: Enquiries from our website and Instagram sit unanswered for a day
Lots of tours, few sign-ups
Occupancy dropped and I don’t know why
Meeting rooms are double-booked
Members use meeting rooms more than their credits and we never charge
Monthly invoices are made by hand and some members get missed
Members pay late and we keep letting them in

Members leave after three months
Wi-Fi complaints are our number one issue
AC and maintenance issues take days to fix
Cleaning checklists aren’t followed
Electricity bill keeps going up
Rent is fixed but we can’t tell which floor or location is profitable
Ex-members still have working access cards
Things go missing from the pantry and members’ desks
Mail and parcels for virtual office members get lost

Two locations run on different spreadsheets

occupancy: How many desks and offices do you have, and roughly how full are you now?
enquiries: How quickly does someone respond and offer a tour?
conversion: Out of the people who tour, how many sign up?
What do the others usually say?
bookings: How are meeting rooms booked today?
billing: How do you invoice members each month?
What happens when someone pays late?
retention: How long do members typically stay?
Do you know why they leave?
facilities: What do members complain about most?
How quickly do issues get fixed?
access: How are access cards issued and switched off?
Are there cards still active for people who left?
locations: If you have more than one site, how do you compare them?
growth: What would need to be true before you open another space?

seasons: - Pakistan: demand from freelancers and remote workers for international clients rises with load-shedding and internet issues at home (summer); university graduation season brings startups; Ramadan changes hours. - UAE: September–January is peak for new members and licence-linked flexi desks; summer sees members travel and churn; new-year business setups drive virtual office demand. - Canada: September and January are strong; summer and December slow; winter weather can increase day-pass use near transit. - Event-led footfall during tech weeks and exhibitions.
care: No lease, real estate, legal, tax or building-safety advice.
Never collect members’ names, IDs, company documents, access codes or Wi-Fi passwords.
Decline fake tenancy contracts or addresses used to obtain visas or licences improperly.
Fire, electrical, gas or medical emergencies on site → pi stops and points to emergency services.
CCTV and access logs: note operational gaps; decline covert monitoring of members.
Member disputes: note, don’t take sides.
build_ideas: Enquiry inbox from website, social and WhatsApp with tour booking and follow-up reminders
Occupancy board per location: every desk and office with status (sold, available, notice given)
Meeting room booking via web or WhatsApp with credits per member and automatic overage charges
Recurring billing with automatic invoices, payment links and late-payment reminders
Membership register with start, notice and renewal dates and deposit status
Move-out checklist: access card deactivation, deposit settlement, mail redirect
Maintenance ticketing from members via WhatsApp with tracking until fixed
Cleaning and facilities checklists on phone with timestamps
Mail and parcel log for virtual office members with notification on arrival
Member feedback pulse and exit reasons
Location dashboard: occupancy, revenue, costs, collections, complaints

exchange.text: Our occupancy is around 60 percent and it’s been stuck there for months.
That’s a frustrating plateau, especially with rent fixed — noted. Where are most of your enquiries coming from at the moment?
Instagram, Google, and a couple of listing websites.
Noted, Instagram, Google and listings. When someone enquires, how quickly do they usually hear back?
Depends who’s on the front desk — sometimes same hour, sometimes next day.
Understood, response time depends on who’s on shift — I’ve noted that. Of the people who come for a tour, roughly how many end up signing?
